candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies, printed p.12 / PDF p.16: educate clients about medications; identify adverse effects and monitor/evaluate medication therapy
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — tamoxifen adverse-effect teaching / uterine malignancy warning
candidate.educational_objective: Teach clients receiving tamoxifen to report abnormal vaginal bleeding or bloody discharge promptly because tamoxifen is associated with uterine malignancies requiring evaluation of symptoms.

options.A: Any abnormal vaginal bleeding or bloody discharge
options.B: Only bleeding that begins after tamoxifen has been discontinued
options.C: No gynecologic symptom requires special attention during tamoxifen therapy
options.D: Routine endometrial biopsy is required even when there are no symptoms

candidate.rationale: Current tamoxifen labeling reports an increased incidence of uterine malignancies, including endometrial adenocarcinoma and uterine sarcoma. It states that any patient receiving or who previously received tamoxifen who reports abnormal vaginal bleeding should be promptly evaluated. The label does not limit concern to the post-treatment period and does not support routine endometrial sampling in asymptomatic women. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Tamoxifen is associated with increased uterine malignancies, and abnormal vaginal bleeding during or after treatment warrants prompt evaluation; routine endometrial sampling of asymptomatic women is not supported by the cited label data.
candidate.source_locator: Warnings — Effects on the Uterus: Endometrial Cancer and Uterine Sarcoma: increased incidence of uterine malignancies; any patient receiving or previously receiving tamoxifen with abnormal vaginal bleeding should be promptly evaluated; no data suggest routine endometrial sampling in asymptomatic women is beneficial
candidate.source_organization: U.S. National Library of Medicine — DailyMed
candidate.stem: A client taking tamoxifen asks which gynecologic symptom should be reported promptly for evaluation. Which response by the nurse is best?
